title: How to Break Bad Habits

source.name: VOA Learning English — How to Break Bad Habits
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Imagine you are studying English. Perhaps you are learning new words or expressions. But then you feel the need to check your phone. Perhaps you look on social media.

You return to your studies, only to look again at your phone a short time later. This process, when repeated many times, could reduce your ability to learn new material. It is what you might call a bad habit – a custom or repeated action that has a negative effect on you or your goals.

In our cell phone example, the cue is seeing the cell phone. The craving is the desire or urge to check your phone. The response is checking your phone. The reward might be seeing something interesting on social media, for example.
James Clear notes that to break bad habits, you need to think about each step in the habit-making process.
To break a habit, he writes, you should think about making the bad habit invisible , unattractive , difficult and unsatisfying.

To make your phone invisible, you could hide it away. To make it unattractive, you could think about why it is a good idea to stop checking the phone. To make phone use difficult, you can increase the space between you and your phone. To make your phone unsatisfying, you could make a habit contract . For example, you could ask a family member to watch your behavior and point out when you check your phone. You could promise to pay that person every time you look at the device while you are studying.
One suggestion is to wear a wristwatch. This will limit at least one reason for looking at the phone – checking the time.

“Silence it. Turn it off. Switch on your phone’s Do Not Disturb mode,” she writes. She adds that you can move your phone to a place that is more difficult to reach. For example, you can put your phone inside a backpack.

Wood also suggests another way to think about cell phone use. She says you can add a new, healthy habit onto your cell phone habit. “What about if every time you check your phone, you call one member of your family just to say hello and have a quick … chat ?” she asks.
Finally, Wood suggests one kind of reward you could give yourself for not looking at your phone: reading a good book.

The important thing to remember is that people can change their habits. But they must think carefully about their surroundings or environment. You might decide to stop doing an action, but if such an action is very easy for you to do, you will probably continue doing it.
Habit changes take time. But with patience, planning, and repetition, you can do it.

questions.q: Which of these behaviours would the writer describe as a bad habit?
options: Taking a short break to stretch and rest your eyes in the middle of a long lesson
Picking up your phone again and again during homework, even though it slows your progress
Using your phone once to check the meaning of a new word and then putting it away
Studying English at the same time every evening so that it becomes routine
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: bad habit = hành động lặp đi lặp lại gây hại cho mục tiêu. “look again at your phone a short time later… reduce your ability to learn” ≈ cứ cầm điện thoại lên lại và làm chậm tiến bộ. Ba đáp án kia không gây hại hoặc không lặp lại.

questions.q: In paragraph 3, “the craving” is the part of the habit that is
options: the pleasant result you get afterwards
the action of picking up the phone
the strong wish to do the action
the thing that first makes you notice your phone
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: “the craving is the desire or urge to check your phone” → desire/urge ≈ strong wish. “Seeing the phone” là cue, “checking” là response, “seeing something interesting” là reward.

questions.q: Which action is an example of making a bad habit “difficult”?
options: Asking a relative to keep an eye on how often you use it
Putting the phone out of sight so you are not reminded of it
Moving your phone farther away so it takes effort to reach it
Reminding yourself why it is sensible to stop checking it
questions.explain: Đoạn 6: difficult = “increase the space between you and your phone” ≈ đặt xa hơn để mất công lấy. Out of sight = invisible; nhắc mình lý do = unattractive; nhờ người thân theo dõi = habit contract (unsatisfying).

questions.q: Why might wearing a wristwatch help someone who is studying?
options: The person no longer needs the phone to find out the time
It shows how many minutes remain in the lesson
It stops messages from appearing on the phone
It makes the phone look less interesting
questions.explain: Đoạn 7: đeo đồng hồ “will limit at least one reason for looking at the phone – checking the time” ≈ không còn cần điện thoại để xem giờ. Các đáp án khác bài không nói.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about surroundings and habits?
options: A strong decision is enough to end any habit immediately and for good
Changing your surroundings removes a habit within a few short days
A habit is hard to stop when the surroundings make it very easy to carry out
Where you live matters less than how clever you are at making plans
questions.explain: Đoạn 11: “if such an action is very easy for you to do, you will probably continue doing it” ≈ thói quen khó bỏ nếu môi trường làm nó dễ dàng. Đoạn 12 nói thay đổi thói quen cần thời gian nên “within days” sai.

questions.q: The writer believes that other people can have a useful part in helping you change a habit.
questions.explain: Đoạn 6 (habit contract: nhờ người nhà theo dõi) và đoạn 9 (gọi cho người nhà thay vì lướt điện thoại) cho thấy người khác có thể giúp.

questions.q: Most people manage to change a habit within a month if they follow the advice.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói thay đổi thói quen “take time” (đoạn 12), không nêu con số một tháng hay tỉ lệ người thành công.
